writeup: TIC 232039858 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 6.4789 days. The primary eclipse causes a dimming of 29.36 percent, while a secondary eclipse was detected at 8.2 sigma significance. The automated TESS photometry analysis identified this system with a strong detection signal of 454.9 in the Box Least Squares periodogram, and pixel-level difference imaging confirmed the signal at a peak signal-to-noise of 78.3, though with a centroid offset of 2.1 arcseconds from the target star. The candidate does not appear in any of six variable-star catalogs checked, making it a novel candidate. The machine-learning screening score of 0.58 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a real eclipsing binary rather than a false positive, and no data quality issues were flagged during processing.
